items.title: Store a SecureString parameter and read it with and without decryption
items.kills: "Leaving out WithDecryption hides a SecureString value from the people who can call GetParameter."
items.cost: $0. Standard parameters have no additional charge, and the few AWS KMS requests of this task fall inside the KMS free tier of 20,000 requests/month.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day. A standard parameter that stays in the account has no storage charge.
items.read_only_alternative: Use this when you cannot create parameters. It changes nothing. Read the public parameters that AWS maintains for Amazon Linux: aws ssm get-parameters-by-path --path /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest --query "Parameters[].Name" Each name is a path under /aws/service, and each value points to the latest Amazon Linux AMI in your Region. Then list the parameters of your account: aws ssm describe-parameters --query "Parameters[].[Name,Type,KeyId]" A SecureString parameter shows its name, its type and its KMS key in plain text, and no value.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Store a plain configuration value as a String parameter under the path /saa/secrets-t01, with the two book tags.
steps.command: aws ssm put-parameter --name /saa/secrets-t01/log-level --type String --value INFO --tags Key=book,Value=saa Key=task,Value=secrets-certificates-t01
steps.expect: "Version": 1 and "Tier": "Standard", unless your account sets a different default tier.

steps.text: Store a value that needs encryption, a vendor account ID, as a SecureString parameter. Name no key, so the AWS managed key aws/ssm encrypts it.
steps.command: aws ssm put-parameter --name /saa/secrets-t01/vendor/account-id --type SecureString --value vendor-739482 --tags Key=book,Value=saa Key=task,Value=secrets-certificates-t01

steps.text: Read the SecureString parameter with GetParameter, as an application would without extra options.
steps.expect: SecureString and a long string of letters and digits. You do not see vendor-739482.
steps.predict: You stored vendor-739482, and you are allowed to read this parameter. Does GetParameter show vendor-739482?
steps.explain: Unless the call sets WithDecryption to true, [its value is encrypted](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-with-decryption) in the response. Parameter Store [does not perform any cryptographic operations](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-standard-securestring-direct-kms) itself: with WithDecryption, it asks AWS KMS to decrypt the value under the [AWS managed key that Systems Manager automatically creates](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-securestring-kms-keys). The flag is a request option, not a permission: the reader needs kms:Decrypt [regardless of which Parameter Store operation is used](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-securestring-needs-kms-decrypt). Under aws/ssm, that permission does not narrow who reads: the default key [has Decrypt permission for all IAM principals](../facts/parameter-store.md#parameter-store-default-key-decrypt-all-principals) in the account.

steps.text: Fix it: as the same caller, read the same parameter again and ask for decryption. No extra permission was added.
Read the whole /saa/secrets-t01 branch in one call. The recursive option also returns the parameter one level lower, under vendor.
steps.expect: Both parameters. The String parameter shows INFO. The SecureString parameter shows the encrypted string again.

steps.text: Read the metadata of the SecureString parameter. Look for what is not encrypted.
steps.expect: The name in plain text, SecureString, Standard and alias/aws/ssm. Keep secrets out of parameter names.

still_costs: Nothing after the cleanup. A standard parameter that stays costs $0 a day.
The AWS managed key aws/ssm stays in the account after the cleanup. AWS KMS does not charge for the creation and storage of AWS managed keys; requests to the key count toward the KMS free tier.
